coverage_notes:
WHAT IS SOLID. The full 1990 on-field staff is confirmed twice over: Wikipedia's team-season page and, independently and contemporaneously, the Georgia Tech opponent page of Nebraska's own 1991 Florida Citrus Bowl media guide (published for the Jan. 1, 1991 championship game). Both give the identical nine full-time assistants plus Bobby Ross. The Georgia Tech 1991 media guide's all-time "Assistant Coaches" year-by-year list corroborates every one of them with explicit year spans (Baker 1987-91, Bresnahan 1989-91, Friedgen 1987-91, Hendrickson 1987-91, O'Leary 1987-91, Priefer 1987-91, D. Smith 1987-91, Strock 1990-91, Watson 1987-91). That is exactly 9 on-field assistants + head coach, matching the NCAA limit of the era.

SOURCE 2 (SCHOOL SITE ON WAYBACK) WAS IMPOSSIBLE. There was no ramblinwreck.com or any Georgia Tech athletics website in 1990-91; the Web did not yet exist as a public medium. The Wayback Machine has nothing near the title date. Georgia Tech's modern football archive page (https://ramblinwreck.com/football-archive/) offers only two 1990 items - a final-stats PDF and https://ramblinwreck.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/1990-football-roster.pdf. I downloaded the roster PDF; it is a single scanned JPEG of the alphabetical PLAYER roster page (page 9 of the 1990 media guide) with no staff listing at all, so it produced no rows.

SOURCE 3 (1990 MEDIA GUIDE) COULD NOT BE OBTAINED. The 1990 Georgia Tech media guide is not on archive.org, issuu, or the school site (only a 1990 media-guide copy for sale on eBay). Georgia Tech Archives holds it in the physical "Georgia Tech Football Programs and Guides" collection (UP001), undigitized. The best available substitute is the 1991 Georgia Tech media guide on archive.org, which does have a full Support Staff section with tenure statements ("enters his second season", "fifth season", "15th year", "joined ... January 1, 1989"), letting me date people back into 1990 with reasonable rigor. Every support-staff row here rests on such a tenure statement, not on mere 1991 presence.

QUOTE MECHANICS - PLEASE READ BEFORE MATCHING. The two media-guide sources are archive.org OCR text files with hard line wraps and a trailing space on every line. To keep quotes exactly matchable I used single-line exact substrings (no leading/trailing whitespace, no cross-line joins), which means several quotes read as sentence fragments; the full wrapped passage is spelled out in each source's note. I used direct archive.org node URLs (ia802808 / ia802804) because they return HTTP 200 with no redirect; the canonical https://archive.org/download/... equivalents 302 to a rotating node. All 60 quotes in this submission were programmatically verified as exact substrings of the fetched text. OCR typos inside quotes ("staffon", "asa", "Techin", "Homer C, Rice", "staft") are reproduced faithfully and are in the source, not introduced by me.

ONE FLAGGED ROW. Joe Reich is listed as a 1990 graduate assistant on the Wikipedia team-season page, but his own Wikipedia biography gives 1988 as his only Georgia Tech year (1989-1992 at Gettysburg). I kept the row so you can see it, but it is very likely a Wikipedia error and should probably be dropped. Chris Rorke, by contrast, is confirmed by both pages (his infobox reads 1989-1990, Georgia Tech GA).

TIERS I COULD NOT RECOVER.
- EQUIPMENT: no 1990 equipment manager identified. The 1991 guide's equipment manager, Ottie Steien, explicitly "begins his first season ... joining the Tech staff in July of 1991", so he was NOT there for the title. Joe McDonald appears as "Assistant Equipment Manager" in the 1991 staff-photo pages with no tenure information. The 1990 head equipment manager remains unknown.
- TEAM DOCTORS: the 1991 guide names team physician Robert Lambert, M.D., orthopedic consultant Blane Woodfin, M.D., and team dentist Aaron King, D.D.S., and says these specialists "attend all Tech football practices and games" - but gives no start dates, and I found no 1990-dated source. I deliberately left them out rather than assume continuity. Same for part-time assistant trainer Walter Smith and women's-sports assistant trainer Vicky Gamber (Vicky Gamber is documented as handling women's sports, so likely not football anyway).
- STRENGTH STAFF BELOW THE TOP TWO: Lynne Stoessel (Assistant Strength Coach) and graduate assistant Mike Armstrong appear on the 1991 strength staff with no tenure statement; excluded.
- ANALYSTS / QUALITY CONTROL: these job categories did not exist in 1990 college football. Zero rows, correctly. The closest analogue is Lance Thompson, the volunteer coach who also ran "Tech's computer scouting system and statistical breakdown of opponents"; I categorized him as onfield since he coached the strong-side outside linebackers.
- STUDENT MANAGERS: the 1991 guide's all-time lettermen list marks eight people as 1990 student managers, but the OCR of that list is badly degraded (e.g. "Beltiower, Bradley", "Geerigens, Paul", "Bahin, Jim", "Windham, Wilham 1890(mgr)"). Because the names cannot be transcribed reliably I created no rows for them; a page-image read of the 1991 guide's lettermen section would recover roughly eight more names in the equipment/ops tier.
- RECRUITING ADMIN: Karen Palm was Administrative Assistant for Recruiting in 1991 but her bio says she "begins her first season ... after joining Georgia Tech staff last spring", i.e. spring 1991 - not 1990. Excluded.

ONE DELIBERATE EXCLUSION WORTH NAMING. Dave Pasanella, Georgia Tech's Director of Player Development (strength), is closely associated with this team, but the 1991 guide states he "died tragically in an automobile / accident in June of 1990" - before the season began. He was not on staff for the 1990 season and gets no row under the on-staff-at-the-championship-game rule. Jim Lathrop succeeded him and ran the program in 1990.

SCOPE CAUTION. Four sports-information staffers (Finn, Stamus, Zang, George) and athletic director Homer Rice are athletic-department rather than football-team employees; I included them because Nebraska's bowl guide lists them inside its Georgia Tech section for the championship game itself, but filter them if your ring rule is football-staff-only. Jay Shoop's Sports Science role likewise spanned all 16 varsity sports.
